sections.title: Built for pump & valve conditions
sections.live: LIVE H2 → Sealing chosen by medium, not by catalogue. — the best framing on any industry page · the temperature card names no temperature · the slurry card needs the wear boundary

fields.label: H2
lines: Sealing chosen by medium, not by catalogue.
fields.value: Sealing chosen by medium, not by catalogue.
fields.note: [no change] — six words that state the selection principle and the competitive position at once. It is the best section heading on any industry page and the intro delivers on it

fields.label: Intro
paragraphs: Fluid handling covers everything from potable water to aggressive process chemistry. The compound is selected for the medium in contact and the service temperature, then the geometry is matched to your housing.
leads: The compound is selected for the medium in contact and the service temperature, then the geometry is matched to your housing.
fields.note: [no change] — the ordering is correct and it is the ordering a pump engineer uses: medium, then temperature, then geometry

fields.label: Cards ×4
rows: EPDM to +140 °C for water and steam, NBR to +120 °C for oils, FKM to +250 °C for aggressive chemistry. Selection is driven by your medium, not by stock availability. EPDM must not be used in petroleum service.
Adds three figures and the EPDM exclusion

Rotary lip seals and dynamic O-rings specified for shaft speed and surface finish, not dimension alone. Send the shaft finish with the drawing — it is the most common cause of premature lip-seal failure and it is rarely on the enquiry.
Adds the request. The live card names surface finish and never asks for it
Compounds across the full service envelope: silicone from −60 °C, EPDM from −40 °C, FKM to +250 °C — sub-zero ambient through to sustained high-temperature process duty.

Natural rubber has the best abrasion resistance of the eight compounds we mix, and we mould it to your drawing for slurry-duty seals and wear components. We supply both: components moulded to drawing, and rubber sheet lining for casings, sumps and pipework in the same compounds.
fields.note:
Four cards, four cards — no count change, two given figures and two given boundaries.
Card 1 gains three temperature figures and the EPDM warning — EPDM is the compound most often mis-specified into oil service and on a page that recommends it for water in the same sentence, saying so prevents a failure.
Card 2 is the most technically literate card on any industry page and it now asks for the thing it names. Shaft surface finish is the leading cause of premature lip-seal failure and it is almost never on an enquiry — asking for it at this point is worth more than another capability sentence.
Card 3: a card headed “temperature range” containing no temperature.
Card 4 takes the same wear boundary as the mining page and section 03

notes: The three temperature figures render from the locked homepage compound table, same as every other page.

The EPDM exclusion is the trust signal. Telling a buyer which of your own compounds not to use in their service is the same move as the mining page’s wear-liner answer and the oil-gas page’s EPDM warning — it is what makes the recommendations credible.

Shaft surface finish is a genuine AEO opportunity. “What shaft finish for a rotary lip seal?” is a real search with a definite answer and almost no manufacturer addressing it. If the plant can state the Ra range it works to, this card becomes the strongest technical passage on the industry pages.
Card titles are <h3>.

fields.note: 46 words · live is 26 · the live answer is good and the addition is the question it raises. A metering-pump diaphragm is usually fabric-reinforced, and reinforcement is the difference between a straightforward moulding and a two-material one. Q3 is the answer working hardest against the business. A minimum-order FAQ is machine-readable, quotable and stated as policy — and this one carries two wrong lead times alongside it. Inverting it is worth more than any keyword on the page.

Q2 names three approval schemes without claiming any of them. WRAS approved rubber and NSF 61 gasket are searched by water-sector buyers, and a page that explains where the approval actually sits is more useful than one that claims it — and safer.
